text: Lochlann is a name given in Irish myth to a broad northern land. The source sets the name on the home of the Fomorians, who battle the Tuatha Dé Danann. Some readers take the word to mean Denmark and lower Scandinavia. The Fomorian chief city of Berva, as the story names it, is not known anywhere else. The tales may have dreamed the whole land.

okr.objective: Place the name Lochlann at the edges of Irish myth.
